sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:19388
Court No. - 65

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 45510 of 2024
Applicant :- Rahul Sharma Alias Punit Sharma

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Gaurav Dwivedi,Kamlesh Kumar Dwivedi
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard SriKamlesh Kumar Dwivedi, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri R.P. Patel, learned State
Law Officer and perused the material placed on record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 17 of 2024, under Sections 376, 323, 506, 342 I.P.C., Police
Station Mahila Thana, District Agra, during the pendency of trial.
Rahul Sharma
Alias Punit Sharma vs State Of U.P. on 10 February, 2025

1

4.

As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to have established corporeal relationship with
the victim on the false promise of marriage and had taken her valuable ornaments and Rs.1.5 lacs
from her and had subsequently refused to comply with the said promise of marriage.
5.  Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
The victim is aged about 32 years and the applicant himself is aged about 35 years.
The victim is a consenting party as is but evident from the circumstances.
It is next stated that there is no proof of any amount or ornament being taken by the applicant.
6. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
7. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 20.02.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
8. Learned State Law Officer has vehemently opposed the bail application.

9. In light of the judgement of the Supreme Court passed in Niranjan Singh and another vs Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and others AIR 1980 SC 785, this Court has avoided detailed examination of the evidence and elaborate documentation of the merits of the case as no party should have the impression that his case has been prejudiced.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A prima facie satisfaction of case is needed but it is not the same as an exhaustive exploration of the merits in the order itself.

10. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and taking into consideration the settled law of the Supreme Court passed in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690 and Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant-Rahul Sharma Alias Punit Sharma, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to Rahul Sharma Alias Punit Sharma vs State Of U.P. on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176040630/
2 treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

sentences.text: 12. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

13. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
